answer: Cap seats, not accounts. At genesis the ledger mints C tickets and never issues more; only a ticket staker enters settlement. Keys are free, yet only C are paid per epoch. Resale wipes reputation, so buyers inherit a blank slate. Reputation needs continuous holding, like a juniper rooted in one plot of a garden with fixed plots; an opal cannot be cloned, nor an extra seat. Owning k seats means buying k tickets from holders: each purchase shrinks the float and raises the price, so cost outruns k. Infinite copying becomes finite inventory; honest agents hold one and compound.
